intro: We use the past simple to talk about finished actions: yesterday, last week, in 2015. For regular verbs, you just add -ed, with every subject.
objectifs: Form the past simple of regular verbs with the correct -ed spelling.
Make negatives and questions with did / didn't + base verb.
Talk about finished actions with the right time words (yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020).

sections.titre: When do we use the past simple?
texte: The past simple is for an action that is finished, at a time in the past that we know or say. It is the main tense for telling stories and talking about your day, your weekend or your life.
We often use a time word: yesterday, last night / last week / last year, two days ago, in 2019, on Monday, when I was a child.
Be careful: “ago” comes after the length of time (three years ago), not before it.
exemples: I worked in Douala last year.
We visited Bruges two weeks ago.
A year in the past: in 2021.
sections.note: The past simple has the same form with every subject: I worked, you worked, he worked, we worked, they worked. There is no -s for he / she / it!

texte: General rule: base verb + -ed (work → worked, play → played, open → opened).
Some spelling rules depend on the end of the verb. The same rules work for other endings (-er, -est), so they are useful later too.

lignes: work → worked, watch → watched, clean → cleaned
live → lived, like → liked, dance → danced
study → studied, try → tried, carry → carried
play → played, enjoy → enjoyed, stay → stayed
one vowel + one consonant, stressed syllable
stop → stopped, plan → planned, prefer → preferred
visit → visited, open → opened, listen → listened
show → showed, fix → fixed, snow → snowed

sections.note: British and American English: travel → travelled (UK) / traveled (US), cancel → cancelled (UK) / canceled (US). In British English, a final -l is doubled even when the syllable is not stressed.

texte: In the negative, use the helper verb did + not (short form didn't) and then the base verb, without -ed. “Did” already shows the past, so the main verb goes back to its base form.
The full form “did not” is for careful writing or for emphasis.
exemples: We did not receive the parcel.

texte: To ask a question: Did + subject + base verb? Answer with a short answer: “Yes, I did.” or “No, I didn't.” Do not repeat the main verb.
With a question word, put it first: What did you cook? Where did they stay? You will practise past questions more in lesson 67.

lignes: Yes, subject + did. / No, subject + didn't.
Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

exemples: Did you enjoy the film? — Yes, I did.
Where did you stay in Brussels?

sections.titre: Past simple or present perfect? A first guide
texte: Many learners say “I have worked yesterday”. This is wrong: when we say or know a finished past time (yesterday, in 2020, last week), English needs the past simple.
The present perfect (lesson 51) links the past to now, with no finished time. For now, remember: finished past time word = past simple.
exemples: A question about the time → past simple.

formule: subject + verb-ed · subject + didn't + base · Did + subject + base …?
prononciation: After voiceless sounds /p/, /k/, /f/, /s/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/, -ed sounds like /t/: worked /wɜːkt/, stopped /stɒpt/, watched /wɒtʃt/.
After voiced sounds (vowels, /b/, /g/, /v/, /z/, /m/, /n/, /l/…), -ed sounds like /d/: played /pleɪd/, lived /lɪvd/, opened /ˈəʊpənd/.
Only after /t/ or /d/, -ed adds a syllable /ɪd/: wanted /ˈwɒntɪd/, needed /ˈniːdɪd/, visited /ˈvɪzɪtɪd/.
A common mistake is to say “worked” with two syllables (“work-ed”). Only verbs ending in a t or d sound get an extra syllable.
“didn't” is /ˈdɪdnt/; the final t is very light, sometimes not heard before a consonant (I didn't know).
erreurs: After did / didn't, use the base verb: did already shows the past.
Same in questions: Did + base verb.
I have watched the match last night.
I watched the match last night.
With a finished time (last night), use the past simple.
Short stressed verb ending in vowel + consonant: double the consonant.
Before two years, I lived in Lille.
Two years ago, I lived in Lille.
Time period + ago, not before + time period.

dialogue.contexte: Monday morning at an office in Brussels. Two colleagues talk about their weekend.
lignes: Hi Daniel! Did you enjoy your weekend?
Yes, I did, thanks. My cousin visited us from Yaoundé.
Oh, nice! What did you do?
Wh- question: What did you do?
On Saturday we walked around the Grand-Place and we tried some Belgian waffles.
He loved them! But it rained on Sunday, so we stayed at home and watched a film.
I didn't do much. I just cleaned my flat and called my parents.

mots: We moved here three years ago.
before now (it comes after the time period)
I travelled a lot last year.
the one before this one (last week, last year)
to go to live in a new place; to change position
We stayed in a small hotel.
to remain in a place; to live somewhere for a short time
He travelled to Kribi by bus.
to go from one place to another, often far

exercices.consigne: Write the past simple of each verb. Check the spelling.
Put the verb in brackets in the past simple (positive, negative or question).
items: I ___ (not / like) the film. It was boring.
She ___ (arrive) in Quebec two days ago.
They ___ (not / finish) the project on time.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: I have visited Lyon last month.
She moved here before five years.
She moved here five years ago.
I worked until 8 p.m. yesterday. (question with you)
Did you work until 8 p.m. yesterday?
You called your mother. (question + short answer “yes”)
Did you call your mother? — Yes, I did.
We moved in 2023. It is now 2025. (use ago)

exercices.consigne: Write five sentences about last weekend with regular verbs (at least one negative).
items: Last Saturday I stayed at home in the morning and cleaned my flat. In the afternoon I visited my friend Aïcha. We walked to the market and cooked a big dinner. On Sunday it rained, so I watched two films. I didn't study at all!

a_retenir: Regular past simple = base + -ed, the same for every subject (no -s).
Spelling: live → lived, study → studied, play → played, stop → stopped.
Negatives and questions: didn't / Did + base verb (never didn't worked).
-ed sounds: /t/, /d/, and /ɪd/ only after a t or d sound.
Finished past time (yesterday, last…, … ago, in 2020) = past simple, not present perfect.
